title: Evidence Provenance & Proofing Playbook (Cross-Domain Controls)
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary:
This playbook defines how Redwood Inference captures, verifies, stores, and proves the provenance of security and compliance evidence across RBAC/auth, audit logging, data residency/retention, secure SDLC artifacts, and incident response artifacts. It is intended for engineers, security responders, compliance owners, and SREs who produce, ingest, or validate evidence used for internal audits, external attestations, and legal discovery.

Scope:
- Evidence sources covered: authentication/authorization events, entitlement changes, audit logs, system/network alerts, build artifacts, container images, policy approvals, KMS envelope metadata, and incident artifacts (snapshots, forensic images).
- Environments: hosted control plane, Dedicated fleet, Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where evidence collection differs by topology.
- Use cases: SOC audits, SOC2/ISO evidence packages, regulatory e-discovery, customer compliance requests, incident investigations.

Definitions:
- Evidence origin (EO): the system-of-record where the event was generated (e.g., authz-service, iam-provisioner, audit-log-collector).
- Proofing: processes and cryptographic metadata that allow validation of origin and integrity (signatures, checksums, KMS envelope-id).
- Chain-of-Provenance (CoP): ordered set of EO -> collector -> transformer -> archive with cryptographic or verifiable metadata at each handoff.

Ownership & Roles:
- Security (owner): maintains this playbook, approves policy changes, and performs quarterly audits of the evidence pipeline.
- Eng-Infra (collector owner): operates audit-log-collector, s3-audit-buckets, and the ingestion pipeline.
- Eng-Platform (consumers): uses evidence to generate dashboards, runbooks, and customer packages.
- Legal & Compliance (request owner): initiates e-discovery, defines retention holds, approves restricted disclosures.

Evidence Types & Origin Points (examples):
- RBAC/Entitlement Events: origin = iam-provisioner / authz-service; attributes = actor_id, target_resource, change_type, timestamp, request_id.
- Authentication Events: origin = authn-service (OIDC provider), attributes = user_id, client_id, method, success/failure code, timestamp, geo.
- Audit Logs: origin = application services (service-name) -> audit-log-collector, attributes = log_id, seq, timestamp, event_type, payload_checksum.
- Build Artifacts & SDLC Metadata: origin = CI pipeline (ci-runner), attributes = build_id, commit_hash, image_digest, SBOM reference, signing_event_id.
- Incident Artifacts: origin = incident-runner / responder tools (volatility, osquery-export), attributes = artifact_type, capture_id, capture_timestamps, collector_node, hash.

Provenance & Proofing Controls:
- Cryptographic checksums: every evidence object MUST include a SHA-256 checksum at creation and before long-term archival.
- Signing and envelopes: critical artifacts (entitlement changes, release manifests) MUST be signed with KMS-based keys; store envelope-id and key-id in metadata.
- Immutable storage: primary archive = s3-audit-bucket (versioned, object-lock enabled) for hosted; equivalent WORM storage required for Dedicated/Private.
- Tamper telemetry: audit-log-collector records ingestion_ack and storage_ack with timestamps and seq numbers; a reingest/reconciliation job validates seq continuity daily.

Audit Logging & Ingestion SLOs:
- Ingestion success SLA: 99.9% of events from origin accepted by audit-log-collector within 5 minutes of event timestamp.
- Reconciliation SLA: daily job identifies 0 missing-sequence gaps; if gaps > 100 events or > 0.1% of daily volume, alert to eng-infra on PagerDuty.

RBAC & Auth Evidence Capture:
- Entitlement changes MUST record: actor_principal, change_delta (before/after), justification_id (link to approval ticket), request_id, and KMS_envelope_id if applicable.
- Privileged session evidence: for sessions involving privileged roles (role in [admin, infra-admin, key-admin]) capture session id, start/end timestamps, and keystroke-level audit when enabled by policy.

Data Residency & Retention Mapping:
- Each evidence item MUST include residency_tag: {region_code} and residency_policy_id.
- Retention matrix (summary):
  - Authentication logs: 2 years for audits; 90 days hot-searchable.
  - Entitlement changes: 7 years (regulatory); 1 year fast-access.
  - Build artifacts & SBOMs: 5 years if production release; else 1 year.
  - Incident forensic images: retention per legal hold; default 7 years if related to regulated customer.
- Implementation: retention settings enforced via lifecycle rules on s3-audit-bucket and mirrored in metadata store (evidence-index service).

Secure SDLC Evidence Requirements:
- CI/CD publishes immutable release_manifest.json to the artifact registry and signs it with KMS CMK; manifest fields: release_id, commit_hash, image_digest, sbom_uri, signer_key_id, build_timestamp.
- SBOMs and test-signoff artifacts are indexed into evidence-index with tags: release_id, product, environment.

Incident Response: Preservation and Legal Hold:
- Upon incident declaration, the responder runs the Evidence Preservation Checklist (below). Legal must be notified for any cross-border data holds.
- Evidence Preservation Checklist (minimum):
  1) Snapshot relevant audit-log partitions (time range + 15m padding) and copy to forensics-bucket with object-lock.
  2) Record chain: capture request_ids, ingestion_ack, storage_ack, and add provenance marker (preservation_event_id).
  3) Export affected VM/container images to forensics storage and record image_digest + signature.
  4) Freeze retention lifecycle for preserved objects (override via legal hold flag).
- For Private deployments, responders MUST coordinate with customer-side infra to ensure local evidence is sealed and legal hold applied according to customer agreement.

Evidence Verification & QA:
- Weekly verification job: pick sampled objects (1% min; at least 100 items) and validate checksum, signature, and metadata completeness. Failures create tickets in the evidence-triage board.
- Evidence completeness gate for audit packages: package generation requires 100% of mandatory artifact types; any missing items must be documented with compensating evidence and approved by Compliance.

Automation & Tooling:
- evidence-index: central metadata catalog (fields: evidence_id, origin, checksum, ksm_envelope_id, residency_tag, retention_policy_id, stored_path).
- evidence-ingest-cli (examples):
  - Ingest event: redwood-evidence ingest --source authz-service --file ./entitlement-change.json --env prod
  - Verify: redwood-evidence verify --evidence-id EVID12345
- Reconciliation workflow: Kafka topic "evidence.ingest.acks" -> consumer validates ingestion_ack and writes seq state to evidence-index; reconciliation job compares origin sequence to stored seq.

Retention Schedule (condensed):
| Evidence Type                 | Hot Window | Archived Retention | Archive Storage | Legal Hold Override |
|------------------------------|------------|--------------------|-----------------|---------------------|
| Authentication logs          | 90d        | 2y                 | s3-audit-bucket | Yes                 |
| Entitlement changes         | 1y         | 7y                 | s3-audit-bucket (WORM) | Yes          |
| Build artifacts & SBOMs     | 30d        | 5y                 | artifact-registry + s3 | Yes         |
| Incident forensic images    | N/A        | 7y (or LH)         | forensics-bucket (WORM) | Yes        |

Procedures (common tasks):
- Prepare evidence package for SOC audit (owner: Compliance):
  1) Run "evidence-export --scope soc-audit-YYYY" to generate manifest and file listing.
  2) Run verification: "evidence-verify --manifest manifest.json"; if failures, create issue and attach root cause.
  3) Produce signed archive: sign with compliance_signing_key, ship to auditor via secure transfer.
- Handle a missing ingestion gap (owner: Eng-Infra):
  1) Triage alert from reconciliation job.
  2) Attempt automatic reingest from origin or intermediate buffer (run: reingest --from origin --range start..end).
  3) If reingest fails, escalate to Security with exact count, affected services, and time window.

Escalation & SLOs:
- PagerDuty: evidence-pipeline-oncall (Eng-Infra) for ingestion failures or >0.1% gap rate.
- Security oncall for suspected tampering or chain breaks.
- Compliance/Legal for any legal-hold or cross-border disclosure discussions.

Appendix A — Sample Evidence Manifest (JSON sample):
{
  "evidence_id": "EVID-20261112-0091",
  "origin": "iam-provisioner",
  "origin_event_id": "evt-7c8a1b",
  "checksum": "sha256:3ac...f1d",
  "kms_envelope_id": "enc-09a7",
  "stored_path": "s3://s3-audit-bucket/prod/2026/11/12/evid-0091.json",
  "residency_tag": "us-west-2",
  "retention_policy_id": "ret-7y-entitlement",
  "capture_timestamp": "2026-11-12T15:03:22Z",
  "provenance_chain": ["iam-provisioner","audit-log-collector","evidence-index","s3-audit-bucket"]
}

Appendix B — Quick CLI Examples:
- Exporting for a customer compliance request (requires compliance role):
  $ redwood-evidence export --customer acme-corp --window 2026-09-01..2026-09-30 --output /tmp/acme-evidence.tar.gz
- Apply legal hold to a preserved object:
  $ redwood-evidence hold --evidence-id EVID-20261112-0091 --reason "legal_investigation" --owner legal@redwood.com
